rationale: Two days apart, patrols met both halves of the same hole: an unknown listener on an unclaimed port (no row to check against) and a name-matching foreign binary on a claimed port (row exists, identity does not) - port-number or name matching alone cannot distinguish organ from impostor, and the :43904 case remains an open operator escalation.

lesson.title: Verify claimed ports by process identity, not port number or name match
lesson.source: port-trust incidents 2026-08-24/26: unregistered :43906 listener (PID 26824, no registry row) and Aphrodite.exe (pid 18368) holding registered :43904 with a non-atlas command line
lesson.lesson: Port liveness checks decide ownership by matching the occupying process's image path and command line against the registry row - port number alone proves nothing and a process-name collision proves less. A claimed port held by a binary whose name matches the realm but whose invocation does not match the registered launch command is a squatter suspect: report it, escalate to the operator, and never credit the realm as healthy merely because something is LISTENING on its port.
